## 1. One complete operating configuration

The machine consists of an \(N\)-state controller coupled to \(M\) binary thermal units. The controller traverses a ring; its position changes the units’ energy bias. Every controller transition retains its reverse transition and depends on the actual thermal load. Each thermal unit relaxes at a finite rate.

All parameters are static in laboratory time. The model supplies one chemical driving affinity, rather than an externally scheduled protocol. Its full stationary entropy production and chemical power satisfy

\[
\sigma=AJ,
\qquad
\dot W=k_BT\,AJ,
\]

where \(J\) is the net rate of controller turns and \(A\) is the total dimensionless chemical affinity per turn. Internal energies and inventories remain stationary.

The canonical finite certificate is:

| Quantity | Simultaneously specified or guaranteed |
|---|---|
| Thermal units | \(M=10{,}000\) |
| Controller states | \(N=200\) |
| Target occupation | \(10\%\rightarrow90\%\rightarrow10\%\) |
| Acceptable completed stroke | At most 2,000 occupied units → at least 8,000 → at most 2,000 |
| Controller kinetics | Each directed jump rate is at most \(\kappa\) |
| Thermal kinetics | Each unit refreshes at rate \(4\kappa\) |
| Total thermal-update capacity | \(40{,}000\kappa\) refresh attempts per unit time |
| Chemical drive | \(A=4\), distributed over 200 steps |
| Guaranteed good-cycle rate | At least \(1.400213392\times10^{-6}\kappa\) |
| Failed record-cycle fraction | At most \(4.570711\times10^{-6}\) |
| Fuel per good completed cycle | At most \(4.000018283\,k_BT\) |

These are conservative analytic guarantees. The numerical inequalities supporting this point use exact rational arithmetic; they do not depend on extrapolating a simulation.

The rate \(\kappa\) is a supplied kinetic parameter. Assigning it an experimental frequency would require a material implementation.

A good cycle is an actual low–high–low excursion of the thermal bank, allowing intermediate reversals. I proved that its long-time counting rate exists and bounded unsuccessful cycles using actual bad-crossing activity. This prevents a turning controller with an effectively stationary load from passing the completion test.

## 4. Finite precision survives, with a real calibration requirement

I extended the construction beyond exact compensation. The finite point survives all of the following simultaneously:

- Phase-field errors up to \(0.001\,k_BT\).
- Compensated free-energy residuals up to \(0.01\,k_BT\).
- State-dependent kinetic factors between \(0.9\) and \(1\), applied symmetrically to each forward/reverse edge pair.

The resulting exact certificate still guarantees

\[
G_{\rm good}\ge8.9883999308\times10^{-7}\kappa,
\]

with fuel per good cycle below \(4.000044502\,k_BT\).

The important qualification is that compensation must use the **actual fields**. For \(M\) units,

\[
\frac{dF}{dh}=Mp(h).
\]

An uncorrected field error of \(0.001\,k_BT\) can therefore shift a 10,000-unit free energy by as much as \(10\,k_BT\). Keeping nominal compensation while independently perturbing the fields would invalidate the small residual claim.

This removes an infinite-precision premise while retaining the extensive calibration sensitivity. The nominal controller potential also spans approximately \(21{,}972\,k_BT\). That static energy landscape is an explicit construction resource.
